object_description: ten-storey building organized around an atrium
design_condition: Respecting the street line, the tall volume establishes a dense campus presence with roof garden and outdoor spaces intended to compensate for the loss of greenery, though the ground-level open space remains hard and functional.

positive.statement: The setting strengthens the urban-planning idea of the campus by respecting the street line.
The upper-floor routing is promising and offers high-quality workplaces for independent learning.
The facade routes establish an external reference to the city and allow precise orientation.
The classrooms have good spatial proportions and can be easily divided into usable group rooms.
The sports halls can be easily divided without further restricting their room height.
The upper-floor organization around the atrium is compact.

negative.statement: The city-level open space is sober and hard, with little quality of stay.
The roof terrace lacks sufficient information about its technical implementation.
The extra-high perimeter fence prevents an unfiltered view of the landscape.
The sports halls lack daylight and a spatial connection to the entrance floor.
The ground-floor circulation, especially around the multi-purpose room, is unconvincing.
Darkening and effective sun protection are missing.
The facade proposal appears non-specific and schematic.
Building technology and central ecological questions are only rarely discussed.
